title: Recognition of a foreign divorce decree in India
p1:
Got divorced abroad? Does that automatically mean you are legally divorced in India?

Not necessarily. And this is where many people get caught off guard.
p2:
A common misconception is that a divorce granted by a foreign court is automatically valid in India. But Indian law does not recognise every foreign divorce decree without question.

Under Section 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a foreign judgment may not be conclusive in India if certain legal conditions are not satisfied.
p3:
For example, if an Indian couple married under Hindu law and one spouse obtains a divorce abroad without the other spouse properly participating in the proceedings, recognition in India may become complicated.

Indian courts generally examine factors such as whether the foreign court had proper jurisdiction, whether the decision was on the merits, and whether the divorce ground is recognised under the applicable Indian matrimonial law.

The surprising part? A person may consider themselves divorced abroad but still face questions about their marital status in India.

Practical takeaway: Before remarrying in India or relying on a foreign divorce decree for legal purposes, get its recognition under Indian law examined.
conclusion: If a foreign court grants a divorce but the other spouse never genuinely participates in the proceedings, should India automatically recognise that divorce? What do you think?
